html:
Sweden-Norway was the union of the kingdoms of Sweden and Norway under one king, from 1814 to 1905. Each kept its own parliament, laws, army and money, but foreign policy was run from Stockholm.

It came out of the Napoleonic wars. Denmark-Norway had sided with Napoleon, and by the Treaty of Kiel in 1814 Denmark had to give Norway to Sweden. The Norwegians refused, wrote their own constitution at Eidsvoll on 17 May 1814 and chose their own king. After a short war they accepted union with Sweden but kept that constitution. The Swedish crown prince who forced the deal was a former French marshal, Charles XIV John.

Norway grew more confident through the century, with its own shipping fleet and national culture. The final quarrel was over Norway's wish for its own consuls abroad. In 1905 the Norwegian parliament ended the union, a vote of the people backed it, and Sweden accepted without war. Norway chose a Danish prince as its king.
sum: Sweden-Norway was the union of the kingdoms of Sweden and Norway under one king, from 1814 to 1905. Each kept its own parliament, laws, army and money, but foreign policy was run from Stockholm.
